title: A Worm Grows to 2 Feet Inside a Cricket, Then Steers It Into Water

scenes.text: Something inside this cricket is steering it.
A hairworm. It hatches in water, gets eaten by an insect, and grows inside a cricket for about a month.
It absorbs the cricket's fat. Full grown, it measures one to two feet, curled inside a body only inches long.
Then it changes the cricket's brain chemistry. The cricket walks, mindlessly, until it reaches water.
Crickets can't sense water from far away. The worm just keeps them moving until they hit it.
In the water, the worm bursts out, swims away and finds a mate. The cricket was only ever a ride.

description:
Hairworms grow inside crickets for about a month, absorbing their fat until the worm reaches one to two feet long.
Then they boost chemicals in the host's brain so it walks until it reaches water, where the worm emerges to mate. Researchers found crickets do not sense water from a distance.
What is the strangest parasite you have heard of?
subject: hairworm cricket
first_comment: The worm needs water to breed, so it drives its host there. Which parasite scares you most?
